title: Inspiration contracts
description: Generated by libs/contracts/codegen/generate.ts. Do not edit.

Account.description: The signed-in person, as the account settings show them.

email.description: The verified address the person signs in with.

AclChanged.description: Source sync always stores the snapshot in the knowledge store (KnowledgeStore.put_acl_snapshot) in the same transaction as this event, and inlines it here when it is small. When snapshot is absent, access control reads it from the knowledge store by source_id, external_id and acl_hash.

space_id.description: The space the source is mirrored into.

external_id.description: The principal's ID in the source system. Absent for anyone_* and public.

principal_id.description: Canonical principal, once access control has mapped external_id. Unmapped principals are denied.

AclFidelity.description: exact = per-document ACL read from the source; approximate = inherited or partial; connection_scoped = only "whoever the connection can see"; none = no ACL available.

AclPrincipalKind.description: Principals as the source system names them: a user is a person there, which the directory maps to a member. anyone_in_tenant and anyone_with_link are tracked separately because existing oversharing ("anyone in the company with the link") is the biggest go-live risk.

AgentApproval.description: Who confirms before the agent's output takes effect.

output.description: Final output, valid against the spec's output_schema when it has one.

proposal_ids.description: Proposals and todos the run created through propose tools.

principal.description: The identity the agent acts as. Assistants triggered by a member run as an agent principal on behalf of that member; governance agents run as a service principal.

sensitivity.description: Highest label the run may send to a model. Defaults to the principal's clearance.

AgentRunStatus.description: completed = final output produced; needs_approval = output waits for the approver in the spec; max_steps and budget_exceeded = stopped by a limit; failed = error.

max_tokens.description: Total input plus output tokens across all steps.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema the final output must satisfy.

thought.description: The model's short stated reason for the action, kept for traces.

result.description: The tool result as given to the model (possibly truncated).

sensitivity.description: On tool calls, the run's label once the result joined the conversation: the context's label raised by every tool result so far. Kept apart from result, which truncation can cut, so a replay routes later model calls as the recorded run did.

Anchor.description: Where a comment or override attaches on a page.

page_version.description: The version the anchor was created on.

claim_ids.description: Claims of the anchored block at creation, used to re-anchor after regeneration.

row_key.description: Table row key, when anchored to a row.

unit_ids.description: The units the note is about.

held_value.description: conflict and outdated: the value that holds, as a normalized value key ("650 CNY/night"), so a screen can say it in its reader's words.

values.description: conflict: the values in dispute; outdated: the replaced values the documents still state. Normalized value keys.

documents.description: outdated: the titles of the documents that still state a replaced value.

AnswerNoteKind.description: conflict: sources state different values and a person has yet to decide; the answer gives the value that holds meanwhile. outdated: a source the question found states a value governance replaced, and the answer gives the value that holds. thin_evidence: one source, read with low confidence.

context.description: Caller-provided context (the task the agent is doing), used to prune SOP branches.

ApiError.description: The body of every error response.

ApiErrorCode.description: forbidden is a token whose scopes do not cover the route, or an admin write on a space the member may read but not administer; conflict is a directory command older than the engine's copy; too_large is an upload over the size a file may have (status 413), and unsupported_type a file of a type the engine does not read (status 415).

ApprovalDefinition.description: An approval process definition. Feishu definitions give the form and an ordered node list but no branch edges; extraction mines the edges from instance logs.

approver_rule.description: The source's description of who approves, as text.

ApprovalState.description: Whether the source marks this version as authoritative.

actor_external_id.description: Pseudonymized by the connector unless the tenant allows real IDs.

ArtifactState.description: The freshness engine's record for one built artifact. inputs_hash combines the input hashes with the producer's stage, version, model and prompt version.

AssumptionCheck.description: How to re-check one assumption of a research report. The scheduler re-checks only assumptions and marks dependent conclusions at risk when one drifts.

target.description: URL, search query, internal query or metric name.

AuditEvent.description: One audited action. Written by access control; agent calls are audited per call by the agent API.

AuthContext.description: How the session behind a token signed in. It feeds policy only (for example MFA for admin commands), never identity.

method.description: The sign-in method, such as password, email_code or sso.

BlobRef.description: A stored binary object (an uploaded file, an image, a view bundle).

BlockKey.description: Stable key of a block within a page, built from the section path and the block's role, for example "approval-limits/p2". It survives re-renders while the block's meaning is unchanged, and is what comments and overrides anchor to.

BlockOrigin.description: generated = written by the page compiler; override = a pinned human override; human = added by a person.

BlocksChanged.description: Normalization stored a version's blocks and spans. Block and span IDs are stable across versions, so consumers redo only what changed: added and changed blocks hold the new text, and claims citing removed spans have lost that evidence. A deleted document has every block removed.

changed_block_ids.description: Blocks that kept their ID but whose text, kind or heading path changed. A block under a renamed heading is changed although its text and spans are not, since what it says depends on the headings above it.

removed_span_ids.description: Spans of the previous version that this version no longer contains.

duplicates.description: Other current documents of the tenant with the same or nearly the same text.

ChangeEvent.description: A hint that an item changed. It never carries content.

raw_event_id.description: The source system's event ID, for deduplication.

ChangeProposal.description: An edit the agent proposes in response to a comment or a governance finding.

auto_applicable.description: True only for changes policy allows without review, such as typo fixes.

ChartEncoding.description: Maps data fields to visual channels.

ChartSpec.description: A data-bound chart. The renderer shows values on hover and links each point to the claims or query rows behind it.

echarts_overrides.description: Optional ECharts option fragment merged over the generated option.

images.description: Images for vision-capable models (page scans, diagrams).

Chunk.description: A 400 to 800 token retrieval unit with a contextual header.

contextual_header.description: A short LLM-written header that situates the chunk in its document.

acl_tokens.description: The chunk's tenant tokens (access control's chunkTokens). Retrieval pre-filters on overlap with the viewer's tokens, which keeps tenants apart; the chunk's space decides who reads it.

Citation.description: A readable source passage. Sources the viewer cannot read are never cited.

Claim.description: One atomic statement with provenance and two time axes.

statement.description: The claim as one self-contained sentence, conditions included.

subject_text.description: Subject as written, when it is not resolved to an entity yet.

qualifiers.description: Conditions, scopes and exceptions that must travel with the claim ("for tier-one cities", "except during trade fairs"). Atomizing must not drop them.

slot_key.description: The fact slot the claim fills when it states a single-valued fact: its subject entity when resolved, its predicate and its qualifiers, normalized ("hotel_cap_per_night|tier-1 city"). Claims with one slot key state the same fact; their values are the slot's variants and versions (FactSlot).

valid_time.description: When the statement is true in the world ("true when").

recorded_at.description: When the system learned it ("known when", start).

superseded_at.description: When the system stopped believing it ("known when", end).

authority.description: Trust in the best supporting source.

weight.description: Ranking weight from authority, approval state, recency and corroboration.

ClaimDerivation.description: A claim built from other claims (merged, aggregated or inferred).

ClaimEvidence.description: Links a claim to the exact text that backs it.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the span. Must be a substring of the span text.

quote_start.description: Offset of the quote inside the span text, in UTF-16 code units (JavaScript string indices), so span.text.slice(quote_start, quote_end) is the quote.

quote_end.description: End of the quote, exclusive, in the same units as quote_start.

entailment.description: Score from the entailment check that the quote supports the claim.

ClaimOrigin.description: extracted = from a source by extraction; human = asserted in a comment or edit; research = from a deep-research report; merged = combined by governance; mined = from process logs.

source_version_ids.description: Only claims with evidence in these source versions.

ClaimValue.description: A normalized value for single-valued predicates, so that tier-1 conflict detection can compare values in SQL (600 yuan vs 0.06 ten-thousand yuan, 5% vs 0.05).

unit.description: Canonical unit after normalization, for example "CNY/night" or "day".

normalized.description: Canonical string form used for equality checks.

ClaimsData.description: Rows built from claims with normalized values, one row per claim. Either a fixed list of claims or a claim query that the knowledge store runs at refresh time, so new claims appear. Claims the reader cannot see are dropped.

columns.description: Columns to project. Field names map to claim attributes: claim_id, statement, subject, predicate, value_number, value_text, value_unit, value_min, value_max, currency, value_date, valid_from, valid_to, confidence, status, knowledge_class, recorded_at. Other fields resolve to null.

superseded.description: Claims whose "known when" interval closed: superseded by a newer claim, or retracted because their source no longer states them.

comment_id.description: Set for human claims asserted in a comment or edit.

thread_id.description: The first comment of the thread. Absent on the first comment itself.

on_behalf_of.description: For agent comments made for a person.

citations.description: Spans the agent cited in a reply.

CommentIntent.description: How the comment agent classified the comment.

CommentStatus.description: orphaned = the anchor could not be found after regeneration; shown in a side panel, never dropped.

CompanyEntry.description: A company in the account's company switcher.

CompanyMember.description: A member as the company's members page lists them.

json.description: Parsed and validated answer when response_schema was given.

task.description: Dotted task name, "<component>.<verb_object>", for example "extraction.extract_claims". Used for routing, metering and evals.

response_schema.description: JSON Schema the answer must satisfy. The gateway validates and retries once on failure.

budget_key.description: Budget to charge, for example "tenant:ten_x/extraction" or "source:src_y".

use_cache.description: Exact-match response cache. Only used when temperature is 0 or unset.

ComponentName.description: Component that produced an event or artifact, in kebab case, for example "extraction" or "page-compiler". It is also the consumer group name of the component's event handlers.

ConflictCase.description: A suspected conflict between claims, found by governance.

affected_unit_ids.description: Pages, SOPs and models that cite the claims.

batch_key.description: Groups similar conflicts into one todo ("12 price conflicts from the 2025 list").

changes.description: Supports incremental change listing from a cursor.

subscribe.description: Can register push subscriptions (webhooks, WebSocket events).

structured_blocks.description: fetch returns normalized blocks itself, so no parser is needed.

files.description: fetch can return a binary file for the parser router.

process.description: fetch can return approval definitions and instance logs.

ContentHash.description: Hex SHA-256 with an algorithm prefix.

CreateSpace.description: The body of POST /v0/spaces, which only the super admin may send. The engine mints the space's ID; its kind is team.

CurrentMember.description: The account as a member of the company it works in now.

Cursor.description: Opaque pagination or sync cursor. Only its producer may parse it.

format.description: Display format hint, for example ",.0f" or "YYYY-MM".

DataRef.description: Where a chart's or view's data comes from.

DataTable.description: A resolved DataRef, before per-reader filtering. The serving path drops rows whose claims the reader cannot see, then injects the rest into the chart or view.

consistency_token.description: SpiceDB ZedToken, so a later read can ask for at-least-as-fresh results.

DependencyEdge.description: artifact_id was built from input_id at input_hash.

DerivedReadDecision.description: Result of the derived-knowledge rule. readable_support lists the sources the viewer may see; the caller cites only those. Hidden support is never counted or named.

DiagramSpec.description: A diagram compiled from structure (an SOP, an entity neighbourhood, a timeline) by a DiagramCompiler plugin. The LLM may choose what to show but never draws edges itself.

kind.description: Compiler kind, for example sop_flow, entity_graph, timeline, org_chart, approval_map.

nodes.description: Nodes for format "graph", rendered by the client's own graph view.

structure_id.description: The unit the diagram was compiled from.

DirectoryMember.description: The engine's copy of a member of a tenant.

DirectoryMemberList.description: The answer to GET /v0/tenants/{tenant}/members, the engine's copy, for checking drift. Sorted by member ID.

DirectoryVersion.description: The business layer's version of a directory object, increasing with every change to it.

DocBlock.description: A normalized block produced by a connector or a parser. The anchor is stable for the same block across versions whenever the source allows it (Feishu block IDs, page and paragraph index for files), and is what spans and citations point to.

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in page coordinates.

field_key.description: Form field key, for approval forms and records.

DocumentAnnotations.description: The marks of the Annotated view of one version of a document: the current statements resting on its spans that the reader may read, each marked as search marks it (where its value stands with governance, and the statement that holds instead), and those statements that hold in place of an outdated or disputed one. A statement cites only documents the reader may read.

DocumentEntry.description: One document as the Documents tree lists it: its source item and the latest version the engine holds. Built by source sync from what it last stored; listed only to a principal who may read the document.

modified_at.description: When the source last changed the document, where it says.

reading.description: How far the engine has read the latest version; absent means read.

needs_parsing.description: True when the version holds a raw file for the parser router.

path.description: Folder or wiki path from the root of the scope.

translation_of.description: The document this one translates, as the source states it: a language version in Feishu, Confluence or Notion, or a folder's "leave-policy.zh.md" beside "leave-policy.md". Knowledge does not depend on its language, so governance counts a translation with its original, never as a second source. A link the engine detects by alignment is normalization's to record, not the source's.

note.description: For a paused or failed document, why, in plain English.

DocumentTree.description: A space's Documents tree as the member may see it, one node per source.

reading.description: The documents in the tree by reading state. While any are waiting or reading, the tree is worth asking for again.

DocumentTreeNode.description: A source, a folder in it or a document, in a space's Documents tree. Sources and folders hold their children and count the documents below them; a folder with nothing the reader may open is left out, never shown as empty or counted.

path.description: The folders from the source's root to this node, the node's own name last; empty for a source.

source_type.description: For a source, its connector plugin name.

document_count.description: For a source or folder, the documents below it the reader may open.

DocumentView.description: One document for its Original and Annotated views: the version shown, its blocks in reading order, and the marks on them.

path.description: The folders from the source's root to the document.

version.description: The version shown, without its stored blob.

DuplicateDocument.description: A document whose normalized text (without whitespace, punctuation or case) equals this one's, or that shares most of its sentences, or a fifth of them under the same title: a copy, a re-export, an older edition kept in an archive or a download. Governance decides which one is authoritative; retrieval answers from the latest edition the asker can read.

exact.description: True when the normalized texts are equal.

similarity.description: Share of the two documents' text that sits in sentences both contain, weighted by length: 1 for equal texts, about 0.9 for an edition with a few changed figures, 0.2 to 0.6 for one revised for years.

EmbedBlock.description: Transcludes another unit (an SOP, an entity card, a knowledge model) by reference.

EmbedInputType.description: Qwen3-Embedding and similar models embed queries with an instruction prefix and documents without.

Entity.description: A person, department, product, supplier, system or other thing claims talk about.

entity_type.description: Core types are person, department, product, supplier, customer, system, location, regulation, document.

external_keys.description: Hard identifiers such as credit_code, employee_id or sku.

EventEnvelope.description: Common envelope for every event, close to CloudEvents.

version.description: Payload schema major version. Additive changes keep the version.

subject.description: Main unit the event is about. The bus keeps order per subject where it can.

correlation_id.description: Shared by every event in one causal chain, for tracing a change end to end.

causation_id.description: The event that directly caused this one.

EventType.description: Dotted event name from the catalogue.

FactSlot.description: One single-valued fact across documents and time, read from the claims with its slot key. Variants are the values current claims state; versions are every value claims have stated, with when the system knew it. Counts and a few representatives, never every claim, so a slot with a thousand statements stays a short read.

variants.description: The values current claims state, the most stated first.

versions.description: Every value claims have stated, the earliest known first.

Feedback.description: report_feedback from an agent or a reader; becomes a review todo.

FileMeta.description: What the parser router knows about a file before parsing it.

FileWritten.description: The answer to PUT /v0/spaces/{space}/files/{path}, which uploads one file into the space's uploads: the document the file is now, with its latest version, and whether this upload changed it. The same bytes at the same path change nothing, so a retry is safe; other bytes make a new version. Reading runs in the background.

GovernanceLevel.description: How much of a source the engine governs. governed: fully extracted, and its claims get owners, review clocks and conflict todos. reference: extracted only on use (a passage that touches a catalogue slot, or one a page or an answer cites), with no owners, reviews or todos; a value that differs from a governed one is a note, never a conflict todo. search_only: never extracted, only searched.

gaps.description: What the knowledge base could not answer, stated plainly.

notes.description: What the reader should know about the answer's sources, in the question's language.

span_id.description: Set when the image comes from a source document.

Inbox.description: A member's open todos on the cards the inbox puts them on, most urgent card first, with what each todo asks them to choose between.

topic.description: The topic the card is about, when it has one.

InboxCardKind.description: review: an owner's todos about one topic in one week. notes: an owner's notes of one week. campaign: a space's first reviews of one topic. steward: todos of a topic nobody owns.

fact_label.description: What the fact a conflict or a note is about is called in the tenant's predicate catalogue ("Hotel cap per night"); the slot's qualifiers are its scope.

statements.description: The statements the todo is about (its claims), as the member may read them, in the todo's order: for a conflict, the best statement of each value, the proposed one first.

choices.description: The resolutions the todo offers, in its order; for a conflict, the proposed value first.

IndexFilter.description: Pushed into the search index as a pre-filter. A row matches when its space is in space_ids, its acl_tokens overlap principal_tokens, and its sensitivity is at most max_sensitivity. Results are still re-checked before they leave the server.

principal_tokens.description: The tenant tokens the viewer matches: tenant:<tenant ID> for a member of the tenant, system:<tenant ID> for its services. Spaces decide who reads a row; the tokens keep tenants apart inside the index.

InlineData.description: Rows embedded in the page. Each row may cite claims.

rows.description: One array of values per row, in column order.

row_claim_ids.description: Claims behind each row, parallel to rows. Rows a reader cannot see are dropped.

InlineMarkdown.description: One line of CommonMark inline syntax: emphasis, strong, code, links and strikethrough only. Links to knowledge units use the scheme "inspiration://<unit id>". No raw HTML.

Interval.description: Half-open time interval [start, end). A missing bound means open.

Invite.description: An invite link of the current company. Anyone who opens it signed in joins as a member, until it expires or a super admin revokes it. Only a hash of its code is kept, so the link itself is shown once, in InviteLink.

joined.description: How many people joined through the link.

InviteLink.description: The answer to POST /api/invites, the one time the link is shown.

InviteList.description: GET /api/invites, the current company's links that are still open, newest first.

JoinPreview.description: GET /api/join/{code}, open to anyone holding the link, before they sign in: what they would join. Unknown, expired and revoked codes answer 404 alike. It names no ID, so the page can show all of it.

KnowledgeClass.description: Selects the default TTL used by staleness scoring. Known values: policy, product, pricing, org, process, technical, market, general. Tenants may add their own.

KnowledgeModel.description: A formula, decision table or KPI definition whose assumptions are claims.

expression.description: Formula in a small safe expression language (arithmetic, comparisons, min, max, round).

role.description: Set on cites edges: whether the span supports, contradicts or qualifies the claim. Only supporting evidence makes a claim readable.

LineageGraph.description: The provenance graph from a unit down to source spans.

Markdown.description: CommonMark plus GFM tables and task lists. No raw HTML.

Me.description: The answer to GET /v0/me: who the principal token names, as the engine's directory copy knows them. admin is true for the super admin, who may create spaces and name their owners.

MemberId.description: One person inside one tenant; unique only within the tenant. A PrincipalId of kind member.

MemberList.description: GET /api/members, the active members of the current company, by name.

MemberRole.description: The engine's internal roles. The product's super admin holds owner, admin, security_admin and auditor together and everyone else holds member; the engine keeps them apart, so a later split of the super admin changes only the bundle the business layer grants. guest is for later.

MemberStatus.description: Only an active member holds rights. Suspending a member or recording that they left drops every grant at once.

ModelTier.description: Capability class the caller needs. The gateway maps tiers to concrete models per deployment, so callers never hard-code a model name.

claim_id.description: The claim that defines or bounds this variable.

NewCompany.description: POST /api/companies. The account that creates the company is its first super admin.

default_locale.description: The language of messages sent to many members; the creator's own if absent.

NormalizedDocument.description: What Connector.fetch returns. Exactly one of blocks, file or process is normally set. When only file is set, normalization hands it to the parser router.

sensitivity.description: The item's own label, when the source has one; otherwise the source's default applies.

authority.description: Trust in this item, when the connector knows better than the source's default.

governance_level.description: The item's level, when the item or a folder above it sets one (front matter, folder defaults, document properties); otherwise the source's applies.

OcrRequest.description: Text and layout recognition for a scanned page or image, served by a local OCR or vision-language model (PaddleOCR-VL, MinerU). Goes through the gateway so OCR is metered, budgeted and routed by sensitivity like every other model call.

image.description: One page image (PNG or JPEG). The parser router splits PDFs into pages.

page.description: Page number to stamp on the returned blocks.

asserted_claim_ids.description: Human-origin claims created because the edit asserts new facts.

OverrideMode.description: replace = show content instead of the generated block; hide = hide the block; insert_after = add content after the anchored block; pin = freeze the generated block as it is now.

OverrideStatus.description: conflicted = sources now disagree with the override; its author has a todo.

PageDiff.description: What changed between two versions, for "what changed since you last read".

removed_block_keys.description: Comments anchored here must be re-anchored or marked orphaned.

PageSnapshot.description: An immutable copy of one page version. LLM regeneration cannot reproduce an old page, so every rendered version is stored. Restoring an old version writes a new version whose blocks are pinned as overrides.

change_summary.description: One-line, human-readable summary of what changed.

version.description: Increases by one each time the rendered content changes.

inputs_hash.description: From the freshness engine. Same inputs, same hash, no re-render.

summary.description: One or two sentences, used in outlines and search cards.

taxonomy_key.description: Stable key of the page's node in the document tree.

sensitivity.description: The highest label among the page's sources.

PageVersionInfo.description: One entry of a page's history, without the content.

PatchSpace.description: The body of PATCH /v0/spaces/{space}, from the super admin or an owner of the space.

PlacedBy.description: clustering: the taxonomy clustering of page-compiler. page: a page cites the statement. member: a person put it there.

Placement.description: Where a statement sits in the knowledge outline: its topic, and the page block that cites it when a page does. A claim has at most one. A current claim of a governed document without one is unfiled and shows under its source section.

member_id.description: The member who placed or confirmed it.

confirmed.description: Confirmed placements never move when topics are re-clustered.

score.description: How close the statement's section is to the topic, when clustering placed it.

PluginName.description: Registry name of a plugin or source type, for example "feishu.docx".

Principal.description: The caller of any API. Agent principals must carry on_behalf_of, the member they act for.

agent_scopes.description: For agents, the permissions the agent was granted. Effective rights are the intersection with the member's.

space_scope.description: For agents, the spaces the agent may touch. Absent means every space the member can read.

scopes.description: What the principal token lets its holder do, on top of the holder's permissions. A principal without scopes came from the engine itself (a worker or a test) and is not limited by them.

max_sensitivity.description: The highest label the principal token lets its holder read (its max_sens). It narrows the holder's clearance and never widens it. Absent means the clearance alone decides.

locale.description: The account's UI language, for anything the engine writes for this principal.

PrincipalClaims.description: The payload of a principal token: a JWT the business layer signs with EdDSA (Ed25519) and the engine verifies against the business layer's published keys (JWKS). The web backend mints one per tenant context, valid at most 5 minutes; OAuth access tokens for agents use the same claims. sub is never a user (account) ID. iat and exp are seconds since the epoch.

aud.description: The engine's URL, or a list that includes it.

scope.description: Scope values separated by single spaces.

obo.description: For agents, the member they act for.

spaces.description: For agents, the spaces they may touch.

max_sens.description: Narrows the holder's clearance; it never widens it.

grant.description: For agents, the grant ID, for revocation.

PrincipalId.description: A canonical principal. mem = member (one person inside one tenant), grp = group, dep = department, agt = agent identity, svc = internal service account. Principal IDs are unique only within their tenant, so anything kept outside a tenant's own rows keeps the tenant with them. The business layer's user (account) IDs never reach the engine.

ProcessSnapshot.description: Process data fetched from an approval or workflow source.

window.description: The time range the instances were sampled from.

ProducerInfo.description: Who or what produced an artifact. The freshness engine folds name, version, model and prompt_version into the artifact's inputs hash, so bumping any of them marks outputs dirty.

name.description: Plugin or stage name, for example "claims.default".

ProductRole.description: A member's role in a company. The super admin runs the company: its members, invite links and spaces. Owners are named on each space, never as a company role.

PublishRequest.description: Bottom-up publishing of a unit from one space into a wider one.

widens_visibility.description: True when readers of the target space could not read some sources. Needs source-owner approval.

PutMember.description: The body of PUT /v0/tenants/{tenant}/members/{member}. Display names only; the engine keeps no email.

PutSpaceAudience.description: The body of PUT /v0/spaces/{space}/audience: the whole audience apart from the owners, which only PUT /v0/spaces/{space}/owners changes. An owner grant in it answers 400. An owner of the space may set any audience; the super admin may only remove grants.

PutSpaceOwners.description: The body of PUT /v0/spaces/{space}/owners, which only the super admin may send. It replaces the owners.

PutTenant.description: The body of PUT /v0/tenants/{tenant}. It creates the tenant or updates it, and registers the calling service as the tenant's service.

QueryData.description: Rows from a registered query against a connected system (never free SQL from a page). The provider runs it with the reader's or the page's permissions, and the result is cached as a snapshot.

provider.description: Data provider plugin, for example "jiandaoyun.records" or "sql.readonly".

QuoteBlock.description: A verbatim passage from a source, shown with its citation.

ReadingState.description: How far the engine has read a document's latest version. waiting: not parsed yet. reading: parsed and searchable, its statements being read. read: done, and a reference document is read further where a page or an answer uses it. paused: the company's reading budget for the day is spent, or the reading model could not be reached, and reading carries on by itself once the next day's budget starts or the model answers; the note says which, and the version is searchable meanwhile. failed: the file could not be read, and the note says why.

RefreshMode.description: on_rebuild = refreshed when the page rebuilds; scheduled = also on a schedule; on_view = fetched when a reader opens the page, within max_age.

Relation.description: An edge between two entities. Every edge is backed by at least one claim.

RenderReport.description: The views component's headless Chromium check, attached to the approval todo so the approver sees the real render: no console errors, no horizontal overflow at phone or desktop width, readable in both themes, no crash on empty or very large data.

scores.description: One relevance score per input document, in input order.

ResearchReport.description: What the deep research runner (research) emits. It enters the system as a source of type "inspiration.research": the report text becomes a source version, and its conclusions and assumptions become claims with origin "research".

ResolveTodo.description: How the member resolves a todo assigned to them: done with one of the resolutions it offers, or dismissed. The response is the closed Todo.

with.description: The key of the chosen resolution.

id.description: The resource's ID. Documents use "<source id>:<external id>", because source documents have no Inspiration ID of their own.

ReviewDue.description: Freshness says units need a look, not what is wrong with them. Collaboration turns it into a todo, merging requests with the same dedupe_key into one open todo as it does for todo.requested; research may re-check the units itself.

reason.description: One plain sentence for the reviewer.

cause_ids.description: For evidence_changed, the units whose change made the review due.

dedupe_key.description: Requests with the same key are one review, such as "freshness:ttl:<document>".

backlog.description: The review was already due when freshness first saw the document, as most are on a tenant's first sweep: work for a first-review campaign, not for an owner's inbox.

ReviewDueKind.description: ttl: the review interval of the units' knowledge class has passed since they last changed. assumption: a day a plan or assumption they state has come. verification_expiry: a person's verification ran out. evidence_changed: a document they repeat changed and they did not.

RoleChange.description: PUT /api/members/{member}/role, by a super admin. A change that would leave the company with no super admin answers 409.

RunId.description: One pipeline run (a compile, a governance sweep, a research run).

SampleCompany.description: A company with sample documents, to look around before uploading one's own. POST /api/session with its tenant_id opens it: the account joins it as a member who only reads, so the engine refuses every change there. It is never one of the account's companies, and its members are not listed.

Scope.description: A grant a principal token carries. knowledge.read reads; knowledge.propose resolves todos, syncs a source and proposes changes; knowledge.write and comments.write are for agents acting on a member's request; provision.directory provisions tenants and members, for the business layer's tenancy service.

ScopeSpec.description: What part of a source to ingest. The connector defines kind and options.

ids.description: External IDs of the roots to ingest (spaces, folders, approval definitions).

include.description: Glob patterns on the source path.

valid_at.description: Only knowledge true at this time.

known_at.description: Only knowledge the system held at this time (audit queries).

slot_key.description: The fact slot a claim fills.

standing.description: Where the claim's value stands with governance, for a claim that fills a fact slot.

held_unit_id.description: For an outdated or disputed value, the claim that states the value that holds.

space_ids.description: Narrow to these spaces. The permission filter applies regardless.

token_budget.description: Upper bound on the size of the result as rendered for an agent.

SensitivityLabel.description: Ordered from least to most sensitive. A derived unit takes the highest label of its sources. Model routing never sends content above a provider's allowed label.

SentenceRole.description: claim = asserts something and must cite at least one claim; connective = transition text with no factual content, which carries no citations.

Session.description: Who is signed in, the companies they belong to, and the one they are working in. GET /api/session answers it, or 401 when nobody is signed in; every call that changes the account or the current company answers it too.

companies.description: The companies the account is an active member of, by name.

current.description: The company the person works in now; absent until they create or join one, or open the sample company.

sample.description: The sample company anyone signed in may open, when this site has one.

SignOut.description: The answer to POST /api/auth/sign-out. The session is over; the page goes to next, the identity provider's own sign-out, so a shared computer is signed out there too.

SlotStanding.description: Where one value of a fact slot stands with governance today. holds: the value governance proposes. outdated: a supersession puts the held value in its place (an older edition, a translation behind its original), or a person chose the held value over it. disputed: an open contradiction with the held value, for a person to decide. differs: another difference, such as a scope, a plan or a value only reference documents state.

value.description: The value key, as in SlotVariant.

rationale.description: Why the value stands so, when a conflict case says.

SlotVariant.description: A value current claims of a slot state, and how many claims and documents state it.

value.description: The value key (the normalized value, else its number or text).

claim_ids.description: Up to five representatives, the highest weight first.

source_version_ids.description: Up to five of the versions that state it, those of the representatives first.

valid_from.description: The earliest day a claim says the value holds from.

SlotVerdict.description: What governance says about one fact slot today, for whoever shows its values: the value that holds, whether an open contradiction stands against it, and where every other current value stands. Retrieval marks hits and answers with it.

disputed.description: An open contradiction stands against the held value.

values.description: Every current value, the held one first.

decided_on.description: The day governance decided as of.

chosen_by.description: The person, or the agent acting for one, who chose the held value on a conflict todo. The choice holds while governance would ask the same question.

SlotVersion.description: A value claims of a slot have stated, and when the system knew it: from the first claim recorded with it to the last one superseded, open while a current claim states it.

known_to.description: Absent while a current claim states the value.

Sop.description: A structured procedure. Every step cites claims.

frequency.description: Share of mined instances that took this transition.

support.description: Number of mined instances behind this transition.

Source.description: One connected system or upload area, for example one Feishu wiki space.

space_id.description: The source-mirror space that holds this source's permissions.

default_authority.description: Authority given to versions from this source unless the connector knows better.

governance_level.description: The level of the source's items unless a folder or the item sets its own. Absent: reference, the level of uploads and web pages. The admin picks one when connecting a wiki space.

credentials_ref.description: Name of a secret in the deployment's secret store. Never the secret itself.

SourceBlock.description: One structural block (heading, paragraph, list item, table, ...) of one source version, written by normalization. The id is stable across versions: the source's native block ID where it has one (Feishu block_id, Confluence localId), otherwise derived from the document, the heading path and the text, so a block diff follows the source's own structure. A block that keeps its id but changes its text is a changed block. Spans are the citable passages inside a block; claims cite spans, never blocks.

parent_id.description: The enclosing block (a table for its rows, a list for its items), if any.

anchor.description: Where the block is in the source, as the connector or parser gave it.

heading_path.description: Titles of the headings above the block, outermost first.

text.description: The block's own text (a table's cells joined by tabs and newlines).

ordinal.description: Position in reading order within the version.

span_ids.description: The block's spans in reading order. A heading or an empty block may have none.

SourceBlockId.description: A block of a source document (not a page block, which has a BlockKey).

SourceRef.description: A document or item inside a source.

external_id.description: The item's ID in the source system.

SourceVersion.description: One fetched revision of one item. Immutable once written.

authority.description: How much the source itself is trusted, independent of extraction quality.

governance_level.description: The level this version is governed at, resolved by source sync: the item's, else the source's, else reference. Versions written before levels have none and count as governed.

deleted.description: Tombstone version written when the item disappears from the source.

Space.description: A container that holds permissions. Personal, team, org, or a mirror of one source. owner_id is the first of its owners (SpaceEntry lists them all).

SpaceAudience.description: Who may read a space, and with which role: the answer to GET and PUT /v0/spaces/{space}/audience, for the super admin and the space's owners. The owners appear as owner grants. Higher roles first (the owners), then by principal ID.

consistency_token.description: Set when the answer is to a write.

SpaceChange.description: A document as the latest sync left it, new to the space or an updated version.

SpaceEntry.description: A space as one member sees it: the space, its owners, and the member's own role on it, the highest they hold, inherited from a parent space or not. role is absent when the member manages the space without holding a role on it, as the super admin may. grants counts the space's audience, and is set only in the list of spaces the member may administer (GET /v0/spaces?manage=true).

SpaceGrant.description: One entry of a space's audience. principal_id "tenant" is everyone in the company.

SpaceList.description: The spaces of the tenant the member may read, each with its owners and the member's role; with manage=true, the spaces the member may administer instead, each with its number of grants.

SpaceOverview.description: What a space's maintainers see first: the work waiting in the space, the facts its readers see in dispute, and its documents by governance level with the latest changes, counting only the documents the member may open. Only a member who may administer the space reads it.

work.description: The space's open todos by kind, the most common first.

unassigned.description: Open todos about topics nobody owns, which fall to the space's maintainers.

disputed.description: The facts with an open conflict todo in the space whose readers see a dispute until someone decides, each with its label in the tenant's predicate catalogue.

levels.description: How many documents each governance level holds, in the order governed, reference, search_only.

changes.description: The documents fetched most recently, newest first, at most ten.

SpaceOwnerIds.description: A space's owners, active members of its tenant.

SpaceRole.description: A role on a space, from the least: viewer reads, commenter also comments, editor also edits, steward also verifies and publishes, owner also administers the space and sets its audience. A role on a space holds in every space below it.

SpaceWritten.description: The answer to creating a space, naming its owners or renaming it, with a consistency_token when the engine's graph keeps one (see tenancy.yaml).

Span.description: An exact passage, table cell or form field. Every claim points to spans. A span's ID depends only on its block and text, so a span that did not change keeps its ID in later versions of the document; it is stored once, with the version that introduced it.

source_version_id.description: The version that first contained the span.

ordinal.description: Position in reading order within the version that introduced it.

SpanLocator.description: Where a span sits inside its source version.

char_start.description: Offset inside the block's text, in UTF-16 code units (JavaScript string indices).

char_end.description: End offset, exclusive, in the same units as char_start.

Staleness.description: Staleness is a score, not a flag.

StepBasis.description: Where an SOP statement comes from; shown to readers and reviewers.

SwitchCompany.description: POST /api/session, to work in another company the account belongs to.

SyncReport.description: What syncing a source did: how many items it listed and what became of them. The response to syncing a source now, once the engine has read everything the sync changed.

key.description: Stable row key, so comments can anchor to a row.

cells.description: One cell per column, in column order.

TaxonomyNode.description: A topic in a space's knowledge outline (area, topic or subtopic, at most three levels). Statements are placed in topics (see Placement). Keys are stable across re-clustering and never reused.

status.description: Absent on nodes written before topics had a status; they count as confirmed.

owner_id.description: The member who answers for the topic's statements and confirms its placements.

statement_count.description: Current statements placed in the topic, its subtopics included.

Tenant.description: A tenant as the business layer provisions it (tenancy.yaml). kind, status, default_locale and version are absent only for tenants a corpus stands in for.

TenantKind.description: team is a company. personal is one account's personal library, its own tenant that never becomes a company. enterprise is a team with its own identity provider, later.

TenantStatus.description: A suspended tenant answers no reads; a deleting one is waiting out its grace period.

TextQuote.description: W3C Web Annotation style text-quote selector, the fallback when a block key moves.

batch_key.description: The inbox card the todo is on. Collaboration groups an owner's todos about one topic in one week on a card, at most 20 to a card.

taxonomy_key.description: The topic its units are placed in. The topic's owner, or its area's, is the assignee.

slot_key.description: The fact slot a conflict or a note is about.

week.description: The week it is scheduled in: the week it fell due, or a later one when the assignee's weekly budget of cards was full.

TodoChoice.description: One resolution a todo offers. For a conflict it chooses a value: the value, and the statement of it to show (one of the todo's statements, when the member may read it).

TodoKind.description: note: a value only reference documents state disagrees with the governed one. It asks for no decision: the owner acknowledges it, and it is not counted against the weekly budget. unstated: a new version of a document stopped stating claims, which are kept, marked, until the owner keeps or retires them; source_deleted: the same for a deleted document (docs/design/source-changes.md).

TodoRequested.description: A component asks for a human todo. Collaboration owns todos: it merges requests with the same dedupe_key into one open todo, publishing todo.created when it opens a new one, and a later request with the key replaces that todo's title, detail, priority and units. Requests carry small facts; the detail is a summary, not content.

unit_ids.description: The units a person decides on, such as one claim per competing value.

dedupe_key.description: Requests with the same key are one todo ("governance:conflict:<slot>").

batch_key.description: Groups similar todos in the inbox.

slot_key.description: The fact slot a conflict or a note is about.

resolutions.description: What the person may choose, each with an effect the requester applies when the todo is resolved with it (todo.resolved). Without them, any resolution closes the todo.

withdrawn.description: The reason went away: collaboration dismisses the open todo with this key, and creates none when there is no open one. A later request with the key opens a new todo.

refresh.description: The same question, showing the statements that say each value now (one it showed was superseded): collaboration replaces the open todo with this key, and creates none when there is no open one. It asks nothing new.

TodoResolution.description: A one-click resolution offered on a todo.

effect.description: Machine-readable effect, interpreted by the todo's producer.

TodoResolved.description: A person, or an agent acting for one, closed a todo. The component that asked for it applies the chosen resolution's effect; the others ignore it. A todo the requester withdrew is dismissed without this event.

effect.description: The chosen resolution's effect, as the requester offered it.

ToolEffect.description: read = no side effects; propose = creates a proposal or a todo that a person accepts in collaboration.

token_budget.description: Typical size of the result for an agent, from the MCP tool table.

TopicList.description: The live topics of a space's knowledge outline, ordered by key; areas have no parent.

TopicStatus.description: proposed: made by clustering and not yet confirmed; readers never see it, owners do. confirmed: an owner confirmed it, so re-clustering keeps it and never moves its confirmed placements. retired: it has no statements left; its key is not reused.

TopicView.description: One topic as the member may read it: its current statements and its subtopics', and those of every other value of the facts they fill, wherever they are stated, all marked as search marks them; the statements that hold in place of the outdated and disputed ones; and the facts.

facts.description: The fact slots the statements fill, each with its label in the tenant's predicate catalogue.

UiLocale.description: The account's language, for the web app and for anything the engine writes for it.

Unchanged.description: Connector.fetch result when the known version is still current.

UnitId.description: Any addressable knowledge unit. Used wherever a field can point at several kinds, such as lineage, freshness dependencies, todos and search hits.

widened.description: True when the publish widened who can see the unit.

Unstated.description: The source stopped stating a claim: a later version of its document no longer has the passage, or the document was deleted. The claim stays current, marked, until a person retires it or the document states it again; knowledge never disappears silently (docs/design/source-changes.md, rule 1).

since.description: When extraction read the version that stopped stating it.

deleted.description: That version is the document's deletion.

UsageRecord.description: One metered call, written for every request including failures. Feeds the cost dashboard.

Version.description: What a connector knows about an item's revision. Content, metadata and ACL are hashed separately, so a permission change never triggers re-embedding.

fallback.description: Static block (usually a table or a chart) shown until the view version is approved, and in export, print and clients that cannot run views. Never a view.

ViewCapability.description: What a view may ask its host to do through postMessage. navigate = open a unit; ask = ask a grounded question answered with the viewer's permissions; comment = start a comment on the page; download = offer a file the view built; fullscreen. A view never gets network access.

data.description: Payload matching the view's data_schema, already filtered for the viewer.

ViewSpec.description: One version of one view: either a template plus configuration, or generated or hand-written code. Only approved versions are served to readers; until then the block's fallback is shown.

template_id.description: Set when the view uses a registry template.

template_config.description: Template options, validated by the template.

code.description: Single-file HTML bundle, for generated or hand-written views.

created_by.description: The person or the agent (the view generator) that wrote this version.

ViewStatus.description: draft = created; checked = passed the render check; approved = a person approved it; rejected.

ViewTemplate.description: A reusable view shipped with the product (SOP step navigator, decision tree, comparison matrix...). The bundle is one HTML file with inline CSS and JS.

data_schema.description: JSON Schema of the payload the view expects in insp.init and insp.data.

ViewTemplateId.description: A view template name, for example "sop.step_navigator".
